description: Bitcoin only, beta. The BTC spot price with the change TSP reports beside it (`spot.delta_pct`, in percent; TSP says it is the exchange-reported change over a rolling day), the trend, direction and confidence on each of thirteen timeframes with their consensus, each timeframe's direction recomputed every minute (`live`), the bull, base and bear cases with their probabilities for three horizons (TSP's own labels for them, `most_probable_arm` and `dominant_case`, are defined in mcw-signals-thesis), and support and resistance by how often they recur. Direction and confidence only: no entry, target or stop is published. Every value carries its own observed time, and `freshness` says how old the snapshot is. Each horizon's inputs are judged at the moment of the answer, each series against its own cadence (judged_on[].cadence_check, and stale per input family; ETF flows by two days since their row was written, and max pain, which has no cadence, by six hours since its chain was captured, as stopped_refreshing judges them). TSP re-runs its timeframe rows about every ten minutes, though a round is sometimes skipped, and each row's `cadence_check` judges its analysis against that at the moment of the answer, its `ok` false past half an hour, three re-runs; `live.timeframes` gives each timeframe's direction recomputed every minute from candles by TSP's own rule (the live price against the mean of the last 20 closes; `distance_pct` is how far from it, in percent), or a null direction with `why`. `live.age_s` is its price's age (roughly 100 to 170 s on a working lane: the price is dated by its own one-minute bar, not when it was read) and `live.stale` is true past five minutes, judged at the moment of the answer; `live` is null when none is stored. Not investment advice.
